"""Sandbox & Capabilities From Scratch — course manifest.

Ten graded stages between an agent that is trusted with whatever its tools can do
and an agent whose power is the *intersection* of three things: what its tools
declare, what its principal granted, and what the world will still afford. The
world is provided: `fleet.py` is J1's verbatim (the injected clock, and nothing
else this course needs from it), `vfs.py` is a filesystem made of dictionaries
that normalises nothing and records every path it was made to touch, and
`tools.py` is the environment — nine tools that each declare the capabilities
they demand and what one call costs, five hosts, three secrets, five principals'
grants and roots, five raw plans, and the four objects that *do* something:
`Meter`, `Wire`, `Vault` and `Audit`, each keeping its own record of what it was
asked for.

The thesis of the whole course is one sentence, and every stage's check asserts
it: AN AGENT'S POWER IS NOT WHAT ITS TOOLS CAN DO, IT IS THE INTERSECTION OF WHAT
THE TOOLS DECLARE, WHAT THE PRINCIPAL GRANTED, AND WHAT THE WORLD WILL STILL
AFFORD — AND THE AUDIT LINE IS THE ONLY PROOF OF WHICH ONE SAID NO. Every stage is
one decision about that intersection: what a tool declares and which refusals a
bad declaration earns, what a grant is and why the answer is a difference rather
than a boolean, how a path resolves before it is judged and why a string prefix
is not a jail, why a host pattern nobody can read is not a policy, what a limit
charges and why the charge is all or nothing before the work, why a secret's
fingerprint may travel while its value may not, what an audit line carries and
why its reason vocabulary is closed, how a call is decided in one order and why a
denied call must not reach the world at all, which numbers are recomputed from
the lines and cross-checked against the world's own record, and what a run's
answer to "what did it touch" actually is. The failures worth preventing are the
ones that look like success: a grant that permits everything because it was
tested for truth, a jail that lets the sibling root through, a limit checked with
`>=`, a denied call that charged the meter, an audit line written after the act,
a report whose numbers came from the run's memory, and a secret that reached the
model base64-encoded with nobody noticing.

Standard library only, offline, deterministic, **ints only** (counters, bytes,
ticks — no floats anywhere): no `time`, no `threading`, no `asyncio`, no `os`, no
sockets, no subprocesses, no unseeded randomness, no module-level mutable state.
Nothing here touches the real filesystem, a real network or a real secret: the
filesystem, the wire and the vault are all modelled as data, a dial is a method
that appends to a list, and a denial is a value the loop keeps going with. That
is why this course can be checked to the byte — and why `agents-from-scratch`
(J4's prerequisite C2), which jails a *real* directory with `os.path.realpath`,
is the course this one stands on: the rules are the same, the subject and the
failures are not.

    python3 codecraft/cli.py run sandbox-capabilities-from-scratch
"""

from codecraft.api import stage

TITLE = "Sandbox & Capabilities From Scratch"
DESCRIPTION = ("An agent's power as the intersection of declared, granted and "
               "affordable: a capability set demanded by each tool and refused by "
               "name when the vocabulary does not have it, a principal's grant "
               "whose answer is the difference and not a boolean, a path jail that "
               "resolves before it decides and never lets the sibling root through, "
               "a network policy of exact hosts with no wildcard a reader cannot "
               "evaluate, cpu/memory/ticks limits charged all or nothing before the "
               "work, secrets that reach the model only as a fingerprint and leak "
               "in none of four encodings, an audit line per call with a closed "
               "reason vocabulary written before the act, a call decided in one "
               "order that a denial never reaches the world through, a report "
               "recomputed from the lines and cross-checked against the world's own "
               "records, and a run whose answer to what it touched is its audit and "
               "not its plan.")
LEVEL = "advanced"
ORDER = 23


# --- stage 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def check_1():
    import os
    import shutil
    import sys
    import tempfile

    HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

    DEFAULT_REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

    COURSE = "sandbox-capabilities-from-scratch"

    def _repo(start=None):
        for candidate_start in (os.environ.get("J4_REPO"), start, os.getcwd(),
                                DEFAULT_REPO):
            if not candidate_start:
                continue
            candidate = os.path.abspath(candidate_start)
            while True:
                if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(candidate, COURSE)):
                    return candidate
                parent = os.path.dirname(candidate)
                if parent == candidate:
                    break
                candidate = parent
        raise SystemExit("set J4_REPO=/path/to/forja")

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        A return, or any other exception, is the mistake `what` names — and a
        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.
        """
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            return str(refused)
        except NotImplementedError:
            raise
        except Exception as wrong:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise AssertionError(
                "%s raised %s instead of %s: %r"
                % (what, type(wrong).__name__, exc.__name__, str(wrong)))
        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    from collections.abc import Mapping

    import stage_01 as s
    import tools as world

    # ---- the vocabulary every later stage speaks --------------------------

    assert s.TOOL_KEYS == ("name", "description", "capabilities", "cost",
                           "target_kind"), (
        "this stage's declaration fields are %r, not the five the course "
        "defined" % (s.TOOL_KEYS,))
    assert s.CALL_KEYS == ("tool", "target", "value"), (
        "this stage's call fields are %r, not the three the course defined"
        % (s.CALL_KEYS,))
    assert isinstance(s.COST_DEFAULTS, Mapping) and tuple(s.COST_DEFAULTS) == (
        "cpu", "memory", "ticks"), (
        "COST_DEFAULTS is %r, not a mapping over the three counters in order"
        % (s.COST_DEFAULTS,))
    assert tuple(s.COST_DEFAULTS.values()) == (1, 0, 1), (
        "an omitted cost counter defaults to %r: a call that costs nothing at all "
        "is a call nobody counted" % (s.COST_DEFAULTS,))
    assert issubclass(s.SandboxError, ValueError), (
        "%r is not a ValueError: the course's refusal is a named error a caller "
        "can catch, and every later stage derives its own from it"
        % (s.SandboxError,))
    assert issubclass(s.ToolError, s.SandboxError), (
        "%r is not a %s: one `except SandboxError` must still catch a broken "
        "declaration" % (s.ToolError, s.SandboxError.__name__))

    # ---- capability: one name, a suggestion, and no second meaning --------

    for name in world.CAPABILITIES:
        assert s.capability(name) == name, (
            "the vocabulary's own name %r is not accepted by `capability`" % (name,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a capability that is a typo",
                       lambda: s.capability("fs:reed"))
    assert "fs:reed" in message and "fs:read" in message, (
        "the refusal of 'fs:reed' does not name it and suggest the real "
        "capability: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a capability the world does not have",
                       lambda: s.capability("fs:teleport"))
    assert "fs:teleport" in message, (
        "the refusal of 'fs:teleport' does not name it: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a capability that is not a str",
                       lambda: s.capability(7))
    assert "str" in message and "7" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-str capability does not name its shape and the "
        "offender: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a capability nobody could have meant",
                       lambda: s.capability("frobnicate"))
    assert "frobnicate" in message and "did you mean" not in message, (
        "the refusal of 'frobnicate' suggests a name anyway: a suggestion that is "
        "not close is a lie, and the distance is two: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a capability in the wrong case",
                       lambda: s.capability("FS:read"))
    assert "FS:read" in message, (
        "the refusal of 'FS:read' does not name it: a name is not folded, or the "
        "policy would match in production and not in the check" % (message,))

    # ---- declares: the demand, as one sorted tuple ------------------------

    assert s.declares(world.TOOLS["read_file"]) == ("fs:read",), (
        "read_file demands %r, not one capability"
        % (s.declares(world.TOOLS["read_file"]),))
    assert s.declares(world.TOOLS["debug_dump"]) == ("fs:read", "net:connect"), (
        "debug_dump's demand reads %r, not two capabilities in sorted order"
        % (s.declares(world.TOOLS["debug_dump"]),))
    assert s.declares({"capabilities": ("net:connect", "fs:read")}) == (
        "fs:read", "net:connect"), (
        "a demand written in the other order reads %r: a demand carries no order, "
        "and a program that compares them positionally answers differently "
        "depending on how somebody typed a tuple"
        % (s.declares({"capabilities": ("net:connect", "fs:read")}),))
    assert s.declares({"capabilities": ["fs:delete"]}) == ("fs:delete",), (
        "a demand handed over as a list is not read as a demand")
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a demand that repeats a capability",
                       lambda: s.declares({"capabilities": ("fs:read",
                                                            "fs:read")}))
    assert "fs:read" in message, (
        "the refusal of a repeated demand does not name it: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a demand that is empty",
                       lambda: s.declares({"capabilities": ()}))
    assert "hole" in message, (
        "the refusal of an empty demand does not say what an empty demand is: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration with no capabilities at all",
                       lambda: s.declares({"description": "x"}))
    assert "capabilities" in message, (
        "the refusal of a declaration with no demand does not name the missing "
        "field: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a demand handed over as a str",
                       lambda: s.declares({"capabilities": "fs:read"}))
    assert "fs:read" in message, (
        "the refusal of a str demand does not name it: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a demand that is not a sequence at all",
                       lambda: s.declares({"capabilities": 3}))
    assert "demand" in message and "3" in message, (
        "the refusal of a demand that is a number does not name the field and "
        "the offender: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration that is not a mapping",
                       lambda: s.declares(("fs:read",)))
    assert "mapping" in message and "got a mapping" not in message, (
        "the refusal of a declaration handed over as a tuple claims to have got "
        "a mapping: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration that is not a mapping at all",
                       lambda: s.declares(7))
    assert "mapping" in message and "7" in message, (
        "the refusal of the declaration 7 does not name its shape and the "
        "offender: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "the world's own teleport",
                       lambda: s.declares(world.TOOLS["teleport"]))
    assert "fs:teleport" in message, (
        "the refusal of the teleport declaration does not name the capability "
        "that does not exist: %r" % (message,))
    fixture = {"capabilities": ("fs:read",)}
    s.declares(fixture)
    assert fixture == {"capabilities": ("fs:read",)}, (
        "`declares` bent the caller's declaration: %r" % (fixture,))

    # ---- parse_tool: the record, its defaults, its refusals ---------------

    record = s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",)})
    assert tuple(record) == s.TOOL_KEYS, (
        "a parsed declaration carries %r, not exactly TOOL_KEYS in order"
        % (tuple(record),))
    assert record == {"name": "reader", "description": "",
                      "capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                      "cost": {"cpu": 1, "memory": 0, "ticks": 1},
                      "target_kind": "none"}, (
        "a minimal declaration parses to %r, not to its defaults" % (record,))
    assert tuple(record["cost"]) == world.COST_KEYS, (
        "a parsed cost carries %r, not every counter in declared order"
        % (tuple(record["cost"]),))
    cost = s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                   "cost": {"memory": 8}})["cost"]
    assert cost == {"cpu": 1, "memory": 8, "ticks": 1}, (
        "a cost with one counter spelled materialises as %r: an omitted counter "
        "is a default, not a free one" % (cost,))
    record = s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                     "description": "reads one file",
                                     "target_kind": "path"})
    assert record["description"] == "reads one file" and record["target_kind"] == "path", (
        "a declaration that spells its description and kind does not keep them: %r"
        % (record,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration with a foreign field",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"targetkind": "path",
                                                       "capabilities": ("fs:read",)}))
    assert "targetkind" in message and "target_kind" in message, (
        "the refusal of the field 'targetkind' does not name it and suggest the "
        "real one: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a target kind that is not one of the four",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                                       "target_kind": "socket"}))
    assert "socket" in message, (
        "the refusal of the target kind 'socket' does not name it: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a target kind that is a typo",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                                       "target_kind": "patth"}))
    assert "patth" in message and "path" in message, (
        "the refusal of 'patth' does not name it and suggest 'path': %r"
        % (message,))
    for bad, spelling in (({"cpu": True}, "True"),
                          ({"cpu": 1.5}, "1.5"),
                          ({"cpu": -1}, "-1"),
                          ({"cpu": "1"}, "'1'")):
        message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a cost counter that is %s" % (spelling,),
                           lambda bad=bad: s.parse_tool(
                               "reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                          "cost": bad}))
        assert "cpu" in message and spelling in message, (
            "the refusal of a %s cost counter does not name the counter and the "
            "offender: %r" % (spelling, message))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a cost with a counter that is not one",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                                       "cost": {"cpux": 1}}))
    assert "cpux" in message and "cpu" in message, (
        "the refusal of the counter 'cpux' does not name it and suggest 'cpu': %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a cost that is not a mapping",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                                       "cost": 3}))
    assert "cost" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-mapping cost does not name the field: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a tool name that is not a str",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool(7, {"capabilities": ("fs:read",)}))
    assert "str" in message and "7" in message, (
        "the refusal of the tool name 7 does not name the offender: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration that is not a mapping",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", 3))
    assert "mapping" in message and "3" in message, (
        "the refusal of a declaration that is a number does not name its shape: "
        "%r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a description that is not a str",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"capabilities": ("fs:read",),
                                                       "description": 3}))
    assert "description" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-str description does not name the field: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration with no demand",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader", {"description": "x"}))
    assert "capabilities" in message, (
        "the refusal of a declaration with no demand does not name the field: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a declaration parsed under another name",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("writer",
                                            {"name": "reader",
                                             "capabilities": ("fs:read",)}))
    assert "reader" in message and "writer" in message, (
        "the refusal of a declaration parsed under the wrong name does not name "
        "both: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a demand that repeats, through parse_tool",
                       lambda: s.parse_tool("reader",
                                            {"capabilities": ("fs:read",
                                                              "fs:read")}))
    assert "fs:read" in message, (
        "the refusal of a repeated demand through parse_tool does not name it: "
        "%r" % (message,))
    fields = {"capabilities": ("fs:read",), "cost": {"cpu": 2}}
    before = repr(sorted(fields.items()))
    s.parse_tool("reader", fields)
    assert repr(sorted(fields.items())) == before, (
        "parse_tool bent the caller's mapping: %r" % (fields,))

    # ---- the fixtures: the world's own tools parse to what the world ships --

    for name in sorted(world.TOOLS):
        if name == "teleport":
            message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "the teleport tool",
                               lambda name=name: s.parse_tool(
                                   name, world.tool(name)))
            assert "fs:teleport" in message, (
                "the teleport tool is not refused for the capability it demands: "
                "%r" % (message,))
            continue
        assert s.parse_tool(name, world.tool(name)) == dict(world.TOOLS[name]), (
            "%s does not parse to the record the world ships" % (name,))

    # ---- parse_call: the fields a kind carries ---------------------------

    call = s.parse_call({"tool": "read_file",
                         "target": "/home/agent/notes.md"})
    assert tuple(call) == s.CALL_KEYS, (
        "a parsed call carries %r, not exactly CALL_KEYS in order" % (tuple(call),))
    assert call == {"tool": "read_file", "target": "/home/agent/notes.md",
                    "value": ""}, (
        "a minimal call parses to %r, not to its defaults" % (call,))
    assert s.parse_call({"tool": "env_dump"}) == {"tool": "env_dump",
                                                  "target": "", "value": ""}, (
        "a call to a tool that acts on nothing does not default both fields")
    assert s.parse_call({"tool": "http_get", "target": "api.internal"}) == {
        "tool": "http_get", "target": "api.internal", "value": ""}, (
        "a call to a host tool does not keep its target")
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a path tool with no target",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "read_file"}))
    assert "read_file" in message and "target" in message, (
        "the refusal of a target-less read_file does not name the tool and the "
        "missing target: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a target on a tool that acts on nothing",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "env_dump",
                                             "target": "/home/agent/.env"}))
    assert "env_dump" in message and "target" in message, (
        "the refusal of a target on env_dump does not name the tool and the "
        "field: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a value on a tool that writes nothing",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "read_file",
                                             "target": "/home/agent/notes.md",
                                             "value": "tomato"}))
    assert "read_file" in message, (
        "the refusal of a value on read_file does not name the tool: %r"
        % (message,))
    assert s.parse_call({"tool": "write_file",
                         "target": "/home/agent/report.md",
                         "value": "published\n"})["value"] == "published\n", (
        "a value on a writer is not carried")
    assert s.parse_call({"tool": "shell", "target": "/home/agent",
                         "value": "ls"})["value"] == "ls", (
        "a value on a process tool is not carried")
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call that names no tool",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"target": "/home/agent/notes.md"}))
    assert "tool" in message, (
        "the refusal of a call with no tool does not name the field: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call to a tool nobody has",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "read_fil",
                                             "target": "/x"}))
    assert "read_fil" in message and "read_file" in message, (
        "the refusal of 'read_fil' does not name it and suggest 'read_file': %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call with a foreign field",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "env_dump", "toolz": 1}))
    assert "toolz" in message and "tool" in message, (
        "the refusal of the call field 'toolz' does not name it and suggest the "
        "real one: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call whose tool is not a str",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": 7}))
    assert "str" in message and "7" in message, (
        "the refusal of the tool name 7 does not name the offender: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call that is not a mapping",
                       lambda: s.parse_call(("read_file",)))
    assert "mapping" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-mapping call does not name its shape: %r"
        % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a target that is not a str",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "read_file", "target": 3}))
    assert "target" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-str target does not name the field: %r" % (message,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a value that is not a str",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "write_file",
                                             "target": "/x", "value": 3}))
    assert "value" in message, (
        "the refusal of a non-str value does not name the field: %r" % (message,))

    # ---- the declaration gate: a call to a tool nobody can grant ---------

    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "a call to the world's teleport",
                       lambda: s.parse_call({"tool": "teleport",
                                             "target": "/home/agent/notes.md"}))
    assert "fs:teleport" in message, (
        "a call to teleport is not refused for the capability its declaration "
        "demands: a plan that names a tool no grant can cover must be refused "
        "before the run starts, not survive until a grant is computed: %r"
        % (message,))

    # ---- the plans: what parses, and what must not ------------------------

    for name in sorted(world.PLANS):
        if name == "broken":
            continue
        for entry in world.plan(name):
            parsed = s.parse_call(entry)
            assert parsed["tool"] == entry["tool"], (
                "the plan %r no longer parses to its own tool" % (name,))
    message = _refuses(s.ToolError, "the first call of the broken plan",
                       lambda: s.parse_call(world.plan("broken")[0]))
    assert "fs:teleport" in message, (
        "the broken plan's teleport call is not refused: %r" % (message,))
    unresolved = s.parse_call(world.plan("broken")[1])
    assert unresolved == {"tool": "read_file",
                          "target": "/home/agent/../etc/passwd", "value": ""}, (
        "the broken plan's second call must parse: a `..` in a path is stage 3's "
        "business, and this stage must not pretend to have resolved it: %r"
        % (unresolved,))

    print("check_01: the vocabulary — six capabilities, five declaration fields "
          "and three call fields in declared order; a demand read as one sorted "
          "tuple and refused when it repeats, empties or names a capability the "
          "world does not have; declarations that materialise their defaults, "
          "refuse a foreign field, a bool, a float and a negative counter by "
          "name, and parse every tool the world ships to the record it ships; "
          "and calls whose target and value are decided by the tool's kind and "
          "its demand, with a call to `teleport` refused for its declaration "
          "before its target is looked at")

# --- stage 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def check_2():
    import os
    import shutil
    import sys
    import tempfile

    HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

    DEFAULT_REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

    COURSE = "sandbox-capabilities-from-scratch"

    def _repo(start=None):
        for candidate_start in (os.environ.get("J4_REPO"), start, os.getcwd(),
                                DEFAULT_REPO):
            if not candidate_start:
                continue
            candidate = os.path.abspath(candidate_start)
            while True:
                if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(candidate, COURSE)):
                    return candidate
                parent = os.path.dirname(candidate)
                if parent == candidate:
                    break
                candidate = parent
        raise SystemExit("set J4_REPO=/path/to/forja")

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        A return, or any other exception, is the mistake `what` names — and a
        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.
        """
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            return str(refused)
        except NotImplementedError:
            raise
        except Exception as wrong:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise AssertionError(
                "%s raised %s instead of %s: %r"

        def __init__(self):

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.

        try:

            return str(refused)

            raise

            raise AssertionError(
                "%s raised %s instead of %s: %r"

        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    message = _refuses(s.AuditError, "an entry whose target is empty and unspelled",

    assert "target" in message, (

    assert empty.lines() == (), (

    print("check_07: the audit line — seven keys always written in AUDIT_KEYS "

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        A return, or any other exception, is the mistake `what` names — and a
        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.
        """
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            return str(refused)
        except NotImplementedError:
            raise
        except Exception as wrong:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise AssertionError(
                "%s raised %s instead of %s: %r"
                % (what, type(wrong).__name__, exc.__name__, str(wrong)))
        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.

        try:

            raise AssertionError(

    def _repo(start=None):
        for candidate_start in (os.environ.get("J4_REPO"), start, os.getcwd(),
                                DEFAULT_REPO):
            if not candidate_start:
                continue
            candidate = os.path.abspath(candidate_start)

                if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(candidate, COURSE)):

                parent = os.path.dirname(candidate)

                candidate = parent
        raise SystemExit("set J4_REPO=/path/to/forja")

    def _refuses(exc, what, call):
        """The message of the refusal `call` must raise, or the mistake named.

        A return, or any other exception, is the mistake `what` names — and a
        `NotImplementedError` is re-raised first, so an untouched template escapes
        this check and the runner can say the stage is not implemented yet.
        """
        try:
            got = call()
        except exc as refused:
            return str(refused)
        except NotImplementedError:
            raise
        except Exception as wrong:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise AssertionError(
                "%s raised %s instead of %s: %r"
                % (what, type(wrong).__name__, exc.__name__, str(wrong)))
        raise AssertionError("%s returned %r instead of refusing" % (what, got))

"""Sandbox & Capabilities From Scratch — stage 1: The capability, and the tool that declares it.

An agent's power is not what its tools can do; it is the intersection of what the
tools declare, what the principal granted, and what the world will still afford.
So this stage fixes what a *tool* declares, before anything is granted, jailed,
dialled, charged or audited: a name, a description, the capabilities it demands,
what one call costs, and what kind of thing it acts on — and nothing else.

Every later stage reads these declarations and none of them re-reads a tool out
of its own invention: stage 2 intersects the demand with a grant, stage 5 charges
the cost, stage 8 asks the kind whether a target is a path to jail, a host to
reach or a process to run inside one, and stage 9 looks a tool up by name to say
which capabilities a run actually used. A declaration whose shape is decided
per-stage is a policy two stages disagree about, and the whole course rests on
the opposite.

    TOOL_KEYS       the five fields a declaration carries, in writing order
    CALL_KEYS       the three fields a call carries, in writing order
    COST_DEFAULTS   what a cost counter defaults to when a declaration omits it
    SandboxError    the course's one refusal family (a ValueError)
    ToolError       what a declaration or a call that is not one raises
    capability      one name from the vocabulary, or a refusal with a suggestion
    parse_tool      a tool declaration, materialised without bending the caller's
    declares        the demand a tool declares, as one sorted tuple
    parse_call      a call to a tool this world has, with the fields its kind carries

DESIGN DECISION — why is a demand set that is *empty* refused rather than read as
"this tool needs nothing"?
    Because the two readings are undecidable at the call site and only one of them
    is ever intended. A declaration with `capabilities=()` either means a tool that
    genuinely reaches nothing — which no tool in a real catalogue is — or a field
    somebody forgot to write, and the policy that trusts the first reading hands
    the tool's whole power to every principal. A tool that reaches nothing is
    spelled by its `target_kind` being `"none"` *and* its demand being honest
    about what it reads; an empty demand is a hole, so it is refused, and the
    refusal says which of the two it thinks you wrote.

DESIGN DECISION — why must a demand set be *sorted*, *deduplicated*, and refused
when it repeats?
    Because a set is a value and a list is a mistake waiting to happen. A demand
    carries no order: `("fs:read", "net:connect")` and `("net:connect",
    "fs:read")` are the same demand, and a program that compares them positionally
    answers differently depending on how somebody typed a tuple. So `declares`
    hands back a sorted tuple, and a repeat is refused rather than folded — a
    caller who wrote `("fs:read", "fs:read")` does not know they wrote a set, and
    the next thing they write is `len(caps) == 1`. The same reasoning fixes the
    order of `TOOL_KEYS` and `CALL_KEYS`: an order is a claim, so it is written
    down once, in one place, in the order a reader compares.

DESIGN DECISION — why does `parse_call` read the tool's *declaration* instead of
just checking the name?
    Because "is this tool in the catalogue" and "can this world read what it
    demands" are different questions, and the second one is the one that decides
    whether a call is a call. `teleport` is in the catalogue and demands
    `"fs:teleport"` — a capability the vocabulary does not have — so a call to it
    is refused *here*, before a plan that names it is ever run, rather than
    surviving until a grant is computed and then failing as a missing capability
    nobody can grant. A call to a tool whose declaration this world cannot read is
    not a call, and the run never starts.

DESIGN DECISION — why is a target on a tool whose kind is `"none"` refused rather
than ignored?
    For the same reason stage 3's jail resolves before it decides: the ignored
    field is invisible right up to the moment it matters. `env_dump` reads the
    environment and acts on nothing; a call that names a target for it has
    confused it with `read_file` — and the caller, reading the refusal, fixes the
    tool name, whereas a world that quietly dropped the target would have run
    `env_dump` while the caller believed their file was read. A target is a field
    the *kind* carries, and a field the kind does not carry is refused by name.

DESIGN DECISION — why does a `value` require `fs:write` or `proc:spawn`?
    Because a value is the one field whose meaning is *an effect*, and a tool that
    writes a file or runs a command is the only kind of tool whose value reaches
    something. A `read_file` call with a `value="tomato"` has not been refused;
    it has been silently ignored, and the caller's intent is now a field nobody
    reads. Deriving the rule from the tool's *capabilities* rather than from its
    name means a tool this course has never seen still gets the check right.

DESIGN DECISION — why is the refusal family a `ValueError`?
    Because everything it refuses is *data* the caller handed over: a name that is
    not a capability, a declaration with a foreign field, a cost that is a bool, a
    call to a tool nobody has. `agents-from-scratch` — this course's prerequisite
    C2 — raises `SandboxError(Exception)` about a real filesystem it resolved with
    `os.path.realpath`, where the failure is a runtime fault in the world. Here
    the filesystem, the wire and the vault are all modelled, so a refusal is a
    verdict on a value and belongs to the family Python already catches for that.
    Same name, same rules, different subject — and every stage derives its own
    narrower class from this one so a single `except SandboxError` still sees a
    broken course in any of the ten.

from collections.abc import Mapping
from types import MappingProxyType

import tools

#: The five fields a declaration carries, in the order a declaration writes them.
#: A field outside this tuple is a typo, and a typo is refused by name.
TOOL_KEYS = ("name", "description", "capabilities", "cost", "target_kind")

#: The three fields a call carries, in the order a call writes them.
CALL_KEYS = ("tool", "target", "value")

#: What a counter of `tools.COST_KEYS` costs when a declaration omits it. A call
#: that costs nothing at all is a call nobody counted, so cpu and ticks default
#: to one: an omitted counter is a default, not a free one.
COST_DEFAULTS = MappingProxyType({"cpu": 1, "memory": 0, "ticks": 1})


class SandboxError(ValueError):
    """The course's one refusal family.

    Every stage derives its own refusal from this one (`ToolError` here, then
    `GrantError`, `JailError`, `HostError`, `LimitError`, `SecretError`,
    `AuditError`, `CallError`, `ReportError` and stage 10's `RunError`), so a
    caller can catch a broken course with one `except SandboxError` and still
    read a narrower `except` at the site that knows what it is doing.
    """


class ToolError(SandboxError):
    """A capability, a declaration, a demand or a call this stage refuses.

    The refusal always names the offender — the capability, the field, the
    counter, the tool — and, when the offender is within edit distance two of a
    real name, the real name too, because this vocabulary is exactly where a typo
    silently becomes a default.
    """


def capability(name):
    """One name from the world's vocabulary, or a refusal that names it.

    A name outside `tools.CAPABILITIES` is refused, and a name within edit
    distance two of a real one is refused *with* that name, so a typo is one edit
    away from a fix rather than one search away from a mystery.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("stage 1: implement capability()")


def parse_tool(name, fields):
    """A tool declaration, materialised, without bending the caller's mapping.

    `fields` is a mapping over `TOOL_KEYS`; a key outside it is refused by name,
    `description` defaults to `""`, `target_kind` to `"none"`, an absent counter
    of `cost` to its `COST_DEFAULTS` value, and `capabilities` to a sorted,
    deduplicated tuple — refusing a repeat, an empty demand, a name the
    vocabulary does not have, and a demand handed over as a `str`. The returned
    mapping carries exactly `TOOL_KEYS`, in that order.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("stage 1: implement parse_tool()")


def declares(tool):
    """The demand a tool declares: a sorted, deduplicated tuple of capabilities.

    Refuses a declaration that is not a mapping, one that does not carry
    `capabilities` at all, a demand that repeats a name, a demand that is empty,
    and a demand that names a capability this world does not have — every refusal
    naming the offender.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("stage 1: implement declares()")


def parse_call(call):
    """A call to a tool this world has, with the fields its kind carries.

    `call` is a mapping over `CALL_KEYS`; a key outside it is refused by name,
    `target` and `value` default to `""`, the tool must be in `tools.TOOLS` and
    its declaration must be one this world can read (`declares`). A `target` is
    required when the tool's `target_kind` is not `"none"` and refused when it is;
    a `value` is refused unless the tool demands `fs:write` or `proc:spawn`. The
    returned mapping carries exactly `CALL_KEYS`, in that order.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("stage 1: implement parse_call()")

"""Sandbox & Capabilities From Scratch — stage 2: The grant, and the intersection that decides.

A tool's declaration is what the tool asks for. A principal's **grant** is what
that principal is allowed to hand over. Neither one decides a call: the decision
is their intersection, and the answer to "may this tool run" is the *difference*
of the two sets — sorted, named, and returned as data. So this stage fixes three
things and refuses to blur them: a grant is a value (a principal and what it
holds), the intersection is the decision (`effective`, `missing`, `permits`), and
a policy is the four fields a later guard decides against — who the principal is,
the root it works inside, what it holds, and which hosts it may reach.

    POLICY_KEYS     the four fields a policy carries, in writing order
    GRANTS ALLOWED ROOTS   the three fixtures a policy is assembled from
    GrantError      a grant, or a policy for a principal, this stage refuses
    grant           a principal's capabilities, as one sorted tuple
    granted         what the grants say a principal holds, or nothing
    effective       the intersection of a tool's demand and a principal's grant
    missing         the part of the demand the grant does not cover, sorted
    permits         whether the grant covers the whole demand
    policy_for      the four policy fields for a principal the fixtures name

DESIGN DECISION — why is the answer the *difference* of two sets, when a boolean
would do?
    Because a boolean is the one shape of an answer that cannot say why. `permits`
    exists, but it is defined as `missing(...) == ()`: the caller that only needs
    to know whether the call runs asks `permits`, and the caller that has to write
    the reason into an audit line — stage 8 — asks `missing` and names what was
    not there. A `permits` spelled `set(demand) <= set(grant)` would answer the
    same question and lose the answer stage 8 needs, and the two spellings would
    be free to disagree the first time one of them was edited. One reading of the
    decision, two questions asked of it.

DESIGN DECISION — why does `effective` intersect while `missing` subtracts, and
why is neither of them a check on the other?
    `effective` is `demand & grant` — what the principal actually handed the tool
    — and `missing` is `demand - grant` — what the demand asked for and the grant
    did not have. They are the two halves of one comparison, and both are computed
    from stage 1's `declares` and this stage's `granted`, so neither can drift from
    the other: `permits` is exactly `missing == ()`, and a stage that later wants
    to *report* what a run used (stage 9) reads the intersection, while the denial
    names the difference. Subtracting the other way round (`grant - demand`) would
    answer with the capabilities the tool did not need, which is a set nobody
    asked about.

DESIGN DECISION — why must a grant be sorted and deduplicated, while the
capabilities a *policy* reports keep the fixture's own order?
    Because one of them is a value this stage computes and the other is a
    configuration this stage hands on. A grant carries no order — a set compared

        return dict(self._spent)

    def used(self):
        """A copy of what has been spent, so far."""
        return dict(self._spent)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Meter calls %d/%d cpu %d/%d>" % (
            self._spent["calls"], self.limits["calls"],
            self._spent["cpu"], self.limits["cpu"])


class Wire:
    """The modelled network: a dial per host and port, and a record of each.

    `dial()` refuses a host or a port this world has never heard of, naming both,
    and it records every dial it *did* make in `dialled()`, in order. It does not
    know who is allowed to dial what: that is the policy's job.
    """

    def __init__(self, hosts=None):
        source = HOSTS if hosts is None else hosts
        self._hosts = {}
        for name, fields in source.items():
            if name not in HOSTS:
                raise WireError("no such host: %r%s" % (name, _near(name, HOSTS)))
            self._hosts[name] = {"port": fields["port"], "bytes": fields["bytes"]}
        self._dialled = []

    def dial(self, host, port):
        """Dial a host on a port the world has, and return what it answered."""
        _pick(self._hosts, host, "host", WireError)
        declared = self._hosts[host]
        if port != declared["port"]:
            raise WireError("no such host: %r on port %r (this world has it on %r)"
                            % (host, port, declared["port"]))
        self._dialled.append((host, port))
        return {"host": host, "port": port, "bytes": declared["bytes"]}

    def dialled(self):
        """Every dial this wire made, in order, as `(host, port)` pairs."""
        return tuple(self._dialled)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Wire %d host(s), %d dial(s)>" % (
            len(self._hosts), len(self._dialled))


class Vault:
    """The secrets, and every handle it was asked for.

    `read()` hands over the value on request and records the handle: a vault
    cannot keep a value out of the model's hands, because a vault is a cupboard
    with a log book and not a policy. `meta()` is what a caller may look at
    without reading: the handle and the value's length, never the value.
    """

    def __init__(self, secrets=None):
        source = SECRETS if secrets is None else secrets
        self._secrets = {}
        for handle, fields in source.items():
            if not isinstance(handle, str):
                raise VaultError("a handle must be a str, got %r" % (handle,))
            value = fields["value"] if isinstance(fields, Mapping) else fields
            if not isinstance(value, str):
                raise VaultError("the value of %r must be a str, got %r"
                                 % (handle, value))
            self._secrets[handle] = value
        self._reads = []

    def holds(self, handle):
        """Is there a secret under this handle?"""
        if not isinstance(handle, str):
            raise VaultError("a handle must be a str, got %r" % (handle,))
        return handle in self._secrets

    def read(self, handle):
        """The value, recorded: this is the only way a value leaves the vault."""
        _pick(self._secrets, handle, "secret", VaultError)
        self._reads.append(handle)
        return self._secrets[handle]

    def meta(self, handle):
        """`{"handle", "bytes"}` — everything about a value except the value."""
        _pick(self._secrets, handle, "secret", VaultError)
        return {"handle": handle, "bytes": len(self._secrets[handle])}

    def reads(self):
        """Every handle this vault was asked to read, in order."""
        return tuple(self._reads)

    def handles(self):
        """Every handle this vault holds, sorted."""
        return tuple(sorted(self._secrets))

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Vault %d secret(s), %d read(s)>" % (
            len(self._secrets), len(self._reads))


class Audit:
    """The sink audit lines are written into: text in, text out, in order.

    It holds strings and knows nothing about their shape — the course's stages
    decide what a line is, and `record()` accepts whatever it is handed so that a
    malformed line is the course's own bug to catch rather than the world's to
    refuse.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._lines = []

    def record(self, text):
        """Append one line, and return how many lines are now in the sink."""
        if not isinstance(text, str):
            raise ToolError("an audit line must be a str, got %r" % (text,))
        self._lines.append(text)
        return len(self._lines)

    def lines(self):
        """Every line, in the order it was written."""
        return tuple(self._lines)

    def text(self):
        """The whole sink as one string, one line per line, newline-terminated."""
        return "".join(line + "\n" for line in self._lines)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Audit %d line(s)>" % (len(self._lines),)

"""vfs.py — a filesystem as data, PROVIDED COMPLETE.

The course spans ten stages and every one of them needs a filesystem that can be
read, written, listed and removed from *without touching the real one*: a path is
a string, a file is its text, a directory is a set of paths, and every operation
leaves a record of what it was actually made to touch. Nothing here is timed,
nothing is threaded, and there is no `os`: the whole filesystem is a dictionary,
so two runs of the same call sequence are the same filesystem and a check can
assert the bytes instead of hoping.

It is **deliberately unguarded**, and that is the point: `read()` will hand over
`/etc/passwd` if the tree has it, `write()` will write anywhere the directories
allow, and no path is ever judged against a root. A sandbox is the thing the
course builds, so a filesystem that policed itself would be the answer.

It is also **deliberately unnormalising**. A path that carries an empty, `.` or
`..` component is refused rather than resolved: a real filesystem resolves
`/ws/../etc` the same way the course's own resolver must, and a world that
resolved it for you would be stage 3's answer handed over for free.

The names this module owns:

    VfsError         the module's one refusal family (a ValueError)
    DEFAULT_ROOT     "/home/agent" — the root the course's policy starts from
    SIBLING          "/home/agent-other" — the sibling root a string test lets through
    DEFAULT_FILES    the tree every fresh VFS starts from, path -> text
    DEFAULT_DIRS     the directories that tree needs
    VFS              the filesystem: read, write, remove, list, stat, exists,
                     paths, log, touched

Nothing here knows about jails, capabilities, policies or audits — that is the
course.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from types import MappingProxyType

#: The root a policy is most likely to grant, and the one the course's fixtures
#: are written around.
DEFAULT_ROOT = "/home/agent"

#: The root that *starts with* the default one character for character. A
#: containment test written as `resolved.startswith(root)` hands this whole tree
#: over, which is why it is in the fixture set.
SIBLING = "/home/agent-other"

#: The tree every fresh filesystem starts from, path -> text. The dot-file holds
#: a secret that is also in `tools.SECRETS`, so a leak has somewhere to land.
DEFAULT_FILES = MappingProxyType({
    "/home/agent/notes.md": (
        "# Notes\n"
        "\n"
        "The deploy key lives in the environment, never in this file.\n"
        "Ask the vault for it and pass it to the tool that needs it.\n"
    ),
    "/home/agent/src/main.py": (
        "def main():\n"
        "    return 0\n"
        "\n"
        "\n"
        "if __name__ == '__main__':\n"
        "    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
    ),
    "/home/agent/logs/run.txt": (
        "tick 1 read_file notes.md 47 bytes\n"
        "tick 2 list_dir . 2 entries\n"
    ),
    "/home/agent/.env": (
        "DEPLOY_KEY=sk-live-9f31c2ab7d\n"
        "LOG_LEVEL=info\n"
    ),
    "/home/agent-other/notes.md": (
        "# Notes\n"
        "\n"
        "Another agent's notes. They were never yours to read.\n"
    ),
    "/etc/passwd": "root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh\n",
})

#: The directories `DEFAULT_FILES` needs, plus the parents a `list()` walks up
#: through: a filesystem whose `/home` is missing cannot list `/home/agent`.
DEFAULT_DIRS = (
    "/",
    "/etc",
    "/home",
    "/home/agent",
    "/home/agent/src",
    "/home/agent/logs",
    "/home/agent-other",
)


class VfsError(ValueError):
    """A path the filesystem will not touch, or a file it does not have.

    Raised for a path that is not a string, is not absolute, is empty, or
    carries an empty, `.` or `..` component; for a read of a file that is not
    there; for a `list` of something that is not a directory; for a `write` into
    a directory the tree does not have; and for a `remove` of a missing file.
    Every message names the path it refused.
    """


def _require_path(path):
    """The path this filesystem accepts, or a refusal that says why not.

    A path here is a string that names its components: absolute, with no empty
    component, and with no `.` or `..` in it. Resolving is the caller's job,
    because the caller is the thing being built.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise VfsError("a path must be a str, got %r" % (path,))
    if not path:
        raise VfsError("a path must not be empty: there is nothing to name")
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        raise VfsError("a path must be absolute, got %r" % (path,))
    if path == "/":
        return path
    for part in path.split("/")[1:]:
        if part == "":
            raise VfsError(
                "a path must not carry an empty component, got %r: %r spells a "
                "component twice" % (path, path))
        if part in (".", ".."):
            raise VfsError(
                "a path with a %r component reached the filesystem unresolved: "
                "%r — resolving a path is the caller's job" % (part, path))
    return path


def _require_text(value, what):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise VfsError("%s must be a str, got %r" % (what, value))
    return value


def _parent(path):
    """The directory a path lives in, as a path (`/a` for `/a/b`, `/` for `/a`)."""
    head, _, tail = path.rpartition("/")
    return head if tail else "/"


class VFS:
    """A filesystem made of dictionaries, with a record of what it was asked to do.

    `files` is path -> text and `dirs` is an iterable of directory paths; both are
    copied on construction, so a `VFS` owns its tree and two of them never share
    a file. Every operation that changes or reads the tree appends to `log()`,
    and `touched()` is the sorted set of paths that log names: the world's own
    answer to "what was I made to touch", which is what the course's audit is
    checked against.

    A question is not a touch: `exists()` and `stat()` answer without touching
    anything, and an operation that refused (a read of a missing file) leaves no
    trace either — the log holds what happened, not what was attempted.
    """

    def __init__(self, files=None, dirs=None):
        source = DEFAULT_FILES if files is None else files
        if not isinstance(source, Mapping):
            raise VfsError("files must be a mapping of path to text, got %r"
                           % (type(source).__name__,))
        self._files = {}
        for path, text in source.items():
            self._files[_require_path(path)] = _require_text(
                text, "the text of %r" % (path,))
        self._dirs = set()
        for path in (DEFAULT_DIRS if dirs is None else dirs):
            self._dirs.add(_require_path(path))
        for path in self._files:
            parent = _parent(path)
            if parent not in self._dirs:
                raise VfsError(
                    "the fixture tree holds %r but not its directory %r"
                    % (path, parent))
        self._log = []

    # -- the questions (no touch, no log entry) ------------------------------

    def exists(self, path):
        """Is there a file at this path?"""
        return _require_path(path) in self._files

    def stat(self, path):
        """`{"path", "bytes", "lines"}` for a file, refusing a missing one."""
        path = _require_path(path)
        text = self._files.get(path)
        if text is None:
            raise VfsError("no such file: %r" % (path,))
        return {"path": path, "bytes": len(text),
                "lines": text.count("\n") + (0 if text.endswith("\n") or not text
                                             else 1)}

    # -- the operations (each one logs what it did) --------------------------

    def read(self, path):
        """The file's text, and a log entry saying it was read."""
        path = _require_path(path)
        text = self._files.get(path)
        if text is None:
            raise VfsError("no such file: %r" % (path,))
        self._log.append(("read", path, len(text)))
        return text

    def write(self, path, text):
        """Write the file, create it if it is not there, return its length."""
        path = _require_path(path)
        text = _require_text(text, "the text written to %r" % (path,))
        parent = _parent(path)
        if parent not in self._dirs:
            raise VfsError("cannot write %r: there is no directory %r"
                           % (path, parent))
        self._files[path] = text
        self._log.append(("write", path, len(text)))
        return len(text)

    def remove(self, path):
        """Delete the file and return its old length."""
        path = _require_path(path)
        if path not in self._files:
            raise VfsError("cannot remove %r: no such file" % (path,))
        text = self._files.pop(path)
        self._log.append(("remove", path, len(text)))
        return len(text)

    def list(self, path):
        """The sorted immediate children of a directory, and a log entry."""
        path = _require_path(path)
        if path not in self._dirs:
            raise VfsError("cannot list %r: not a directory" % (path,))
        prefix = path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        children = []
        for name in self._dirs:
            if name != path and name.startswith(prefix) and "/" not in name[len(prefix):]:
                children.append(name)
        for name in self._files:
            if name.startswith(prefix) and "/" not in name[len(prefix):]:
                children.append(name)
        self._log.append(("list", path, len(children)))
        return tuple(sorted(children))

    # -- the record ----------------------------------------------------------

    def log(self):
        """Every operation this filesystem performed, in order.

        Each entry is `(op, path, bytes)` with `op` one of `"read"`, `"write"`,
        `"list"` or `"remove"`: a tuple and not an object, because a check
        compares it to a hand-written list.
        """
        return tuple(self._log)

    def touched(self):
        """The sorted distinct paths this filesystem was made to touch."""
        return tuple(sorted({path for _, path, _ in self._log}))

    def paths(self):
        """Every file in the tree, sorted."""
        return tuple(sorted(self._files))

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<VFS %d file(s), %d dir(s), %d op(s)>" % (
            len(self._files), len(self._dirs), len(self._log))

"""The tiny API an authored course uses to describe its stages.

A course is a directory containing `course.py`:

    from codecraft.api import stage

    TITLE = "Build a Bloom Filter"
    DESCRIPTION = "A probabilistic set, from hashing to false-positive math."

    def check_1():
        from bloom import BloomFilter
        bf = BloomFilter(bits=64, hashes=2)
        bf.add("x")
        assert "x" in bf
        assert "y" not in bf, "a fresh filter must not report false members"

    STAGES = [
        stage(
            1,
            file="bloom.py",
            title="add and contains",
            tags=["hashing", "data-structure"],
            action="Implement add() to set the k bit positions.",
            predict="can contains() ever be certain an item is absent?",
            hints=["bits = bits[:] to avoid shared state",
                   "use one hash salt per position"],
            check=check_1,
        ),
        ...
    ]

`codecraft run <course>` imports this file, runs each `check`, records the
attempt, and hands the result to the adaptive engine. `hints` are optional —
when omitted, the engine generates them from `action`/`predict`.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional


@dataclass
class Stage:
    id: int
    file: str
    title: str
    check: Callable[[], None]
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    action: str = ""
    predict: str = ""
    hints: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    solution: Optional[str] = None   # e.g. "solutions/bloom.py: BloomFilter.add"

    def meta(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "file": self.file,
            "title": self.title,
            "tags": list(self.tags),
            "action": self.action,
            "predict": self.predict,
            "hints": list(self.hints),
            "solution": self.solution,
        }


def stage(id: int, file: str, title: str, check: Callable[[], None],
          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, action: str = "", predict: str = "",
          hints: Optional[List[str]] = None,
          solution: Optional[str] = None) -> Stage:
    """Convenience constructor so course.py stays readable."""
    return Stage(
        id=id, file=file, title=title, check=check, tags=list(tags or []),
        action=action, predict=predict, hints=list(hints or []),
        solution=solution,
    )
